status_note: Launched through the campaign queue as entry 007 on both hosts. av3 started 2026-08-21T21:40:01+0100 and its entry went done at 2026-08-22T03:43:41; av2 started 21:55:01 and went done at 03:39:24. 250 rows per host, 500 merged, 500 distinct keys, no duplicate key, seeds 0-19 complete.
kind: repair campaign (TLSF), single arm, external control
kind_note: There is no second arm. The control is the 780 archived AuRUS repeat rows of 2026-08-14-aurus-h2h, unchanged, read by the same scripts/analyse_aurus_h2h.py. The 499 archived counter rows of that campaign serve as a secondary paired control on (spec, seed).
question: Whether counter at its 2026-08-21 shipping configuration plus the accumulator still trails AuRUS on repair quality over the full 25-family TLSF corpus, after the four changes made permanent since 2026-08-14: the accumulator (37b1f0e), the repaired mutation and crossover grammar (1af9f45, 6e5b710), and the weakening screen defaulting off (e3218a1).
question_note: 2026-08-20-ops-weakening/REPORT.md could read those changes against the AuRUS reference only over the 10 families the sweep-O corpus shares with the head-to-head. Ten families fall in 7 clusters, where the exact two-sided p floor is 0.0156 and every cluster has to point one way; every arm read null there, including the archived arm itself at p = 0.1562 against its own p = 0.0127 over 25. The restriction was a power loss rather than a result -- mean gap 0.222 on the included 10 against 0.224 on the excluded 15 -- so this campaign runs all 25 at full power.
endpoint: Per-family repair-quality rate (implies_ideal over 20 seeds), exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over families at alpha 0.05, with a second read over the 10 correlated-family clusters. PLAN.md sections 5 and 10.1.

unfiltered_per_family.note: The section 10.1 well-separation filter on the AuRUS side moved 2 of 25 family rates: lift 0.167 -> 0.300, lily11 0.900 -> 0.833.

against_the_archive.note: Same script, same AuRUS rows. The archived campaign landed on its outcome 2 (AuRUS higher); this one lands on outcome 3 (no separation). Outcome 3 is a tie and not a counter win.

paired_counter_vs_counter.note: Secondary, not the registered endpoint. It pairs runs against counter's own past rather than against the fixed external reference, and it is the internal measure of what the four changes bought.

decision_rule_firing: Outcome 3 as PLAN.md section 5 wrote it: no separation on either read, p = 0.7549 per family and p = 0.5898 clustered, so the campaign is reported as measured with no re-run and no post-hoc arm.
decision: Reported as measured. The registered hazard fired -- ties rose from 6 families to 8 and n fell from 19 to 17, precisely because counter improved -- and PLAN.md section 6 registered that in advance, so the tie count is reported beside every p rather than read as evidence on its own.

compare_timeouts.note: compare_timeout was raised from the 600 s default to 1800 s for this campaign, on the measured rise in repairs per scoring run. It held.

aurus_side.note: Unchanged from the archive and re-reported, the AuRUS rows being the same file.

known_caveats.run_well_separation: This campaign took the binary default of false. The 2026-08-14 arm ran the per-generation well-separation filter ON, because its config was generated with --pin-vintage, which writes that key from a gen_configs.DEFAULTS entry stale since b101ada made the binary default false on 2026-08-10 -- against that profile's own stated intent of tracking shipping defaults. This is a real difference between the two counter arms and is not one this campaign introduced. The DEFAULTS entry is still stale; --pin-vintage was deliberately not passed here for that reason.
known_caveats.unequal_repeats: AuRUS contributes 30 repeats per family against counter's 20 seeds. That is the archive's design, left unchanged so the comparison stays like-for-like with 2026-08-14.
known_caveats.aurus_only_family: AuRUS scored 26 families to counter's 25. humanoid-741 is AuRUS-only and is excluded from every test.
known_caveats.host_load: Uncontrolled. The two campaigns ran a week apart on the same two machines. The endpoint compares family rates rather than runtimes, so this bears on the wall-clock secondaries alone.
known_caveats.wall_clock_rise: Median wall rose 3.0x and the timeout rate 1.8x against the archive. Both are attributable to the accumulator and to the weakening screen defaulting off, which together push a median of 32 repairs per run through compare against 4.
known_caveats.tie_inflation: A better arm ties more families at the ceiling and the Wilcoxon drops a tied family, so n fell from 19 to 17 as counter improved. PLAN.md section 6 registered this before the run; the sign counts and the tie count are reported beside every p.

follow_up.note: Three arms over this same corpus, seeds, cap and split, with these 500 rows as its outer control. gyro-var2 and lift, two of the four families counter still loses, are what feat/monotone-operators was written for.
